title: The Afternoon Brief: Two new stories widen the day's ledger: Scotland vs. FIFA, LIV's unpaid bills
dek: Scheffler's record win still headlines the weekend, but Monday's new reporting adds a governance revolt against FIFA's Infantino and fresh detail on LIV Golf's financial strain as Saudi funding lapses.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The day's clearest through-line is institutions under pressure to show their books and their votes: LIV Golf's vendors waiting on payment, FIFA's president losing member federations, and Michigan State filling a leadership gap, all playing out alongside a weekend of decisive results on the field.
bottom_line: Monday's new reporting on LIV Golf's unpaid vendor invoices and the Scottish FA's withdrawal from Infantino's re-election bid joins a weekend already defined by Scottie Scheffler's record eight-shot win at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, Cameroon's first Wafcon title, and Amy Hunt's bid for a fourth European Championships gold. The common thread is institutions and athletes reaching decisive or contested moments at once, from FIFA's shrinking base of support to LIV's financial strain as Saudi funding lapses. The reporting is clear on results and on-the-record statements, including Ian Maxwell's stated reasons for Scotland's move and vendors' own accounts of unpaid invoices, but does not extend into what happens next for FIFA's governance committee or LIV's funding talks. Checkpoints ahead include Sunday's mixed relay, next week's BMW Championship, FIFA's response to the eligibility challenge against Infantino, and whether BC Partners finalizes funding for LIV Golf.
body: The picture has shifted since the morning: Scottie Scheffler's eight-shot rout at the FedEx St. Jude Championship remains the weekend's headline result, but two new stories now dominate the broader sports business conversation. LIV Golf vendors report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands of dollars to nearly $100,000 as the league's Saudi PIF funding lapses this month, and the Scottish FA has become the fourth British and Irish football association to withdraw support for Gianni Infantino's 2027 FIFA re-election bid.

On the field, Sunday's results stand confirmed. Scheffler closed with a 4-under 66 to finish at 17-under 263, eight shots clear of Si Woo Kim, the largest margin in the FedEx St. Jude Championship's 68-year history at TPC Southwind. The win secured Scheffler the No. 1 seed into next week's BMW Championship and $23 million in bonus money on top of his $3.6 million prize check. Cameroon beat Malawi 3-0 in the Wafcon final in Rabat, its first title after three prior final losses to Nigeria, with Marie Ngah Manga scoring twice and Naomi Eto adding a third. Amy Hunt won her third gold at the European Athletics Championships in the women's 4x100m relay and was set to attempt a historic fourth in Sunday's mixed relay, while Dina Asher-Smith matched the championship record of seven career golds. In the AFL, Melbourne forward Jacob van Rooyen drew a three-match suspension for a swinging arm strike that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir, sidelining him for Melbourne's game against the Western Bulldogs and the club's first two finals matches. Washington confirmed backup quarterback Marcus Mariota sprained his MCL on a noncontact play in Friday's preseason opener and will miss the rest of the preseason, leaving Jayden Daniels as the only established starter on the roster.

Off the field, two stories about institutional accountability moved forward. LIV Golf's vendor payment problems come as the league's Saudi PIF backing ends this month and it pursues a funding deal with BC Partners' credit division; the league has also filed a WARN Act notice signaling potential layoffs. Communication to contractors has been minimal, with one telling Front Office Sports that LIV's legal counsel has not responded to demand letters. Separately, Michigan State is finalizing the hire of Western Michigan athletic director Dan Bartholomae, who led Western Michigan to a 2025 hockey national title and a MAC football championship and raised a record $21.8 million for the department, filling the vacancy left when J Batt departed for Kentucky.

The why behind these threads varies by story. Scheffler's margin is presented as a result, not explained beyond the scorecard. Cameroon's breakthrough follows a specific history of three final losses to Nigeria, cited directly in the reporting. The Scottish FA's move is explained in Ian Maxwell's own words: governance failures, lack of transparency, and insufficient engagement with member associations, plus his objection to postmatch attention shifting to off-field incidents after a well-received World Cup. LIV's payment troubles are tied explicitly to the end of PIF funding and the pursuit of new investment; the reporting does not establish why communication to vendors has been minimal beyond describing it as such.
No desk boards were available this run, so figures here rely solely on the day's reported stories.

The coming days carry several specific checkpoints. Sunday's mixed 4x100m relay will determine whether Hunt becomes the first athlete to win four golds at a single European Championships edition. The BMW Championship follows next week as the next stop in Scheffler's playoff run. FIFA's governance committee response to a legal challenge over Infantino's eligibility for a fourth term is the next institutional marker, along with whether other confederations beyond UEFA's 55 associations follow Scotland's lead. For LIV Golf, whether BC Partners completes its funding commitment and whether vendor payments resume are the facts to track. Michigan State's official announcement and contract details for Bartholomae would close out that story, and any word on a Melbourne appeal of the van Rooyen suspension remains open.
